title: Developer-local Preflight Spec + Edge-case Signal Sampler for Rollout Gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a lightweight, reproducible preflight runner that developers can execute locally or in CI to surface upgrade-time regressions earlier in the development lifecycle. The runner combines compact smoke tests, a sampled edge-case request generator (Edge Sampler), and a multi-signal regression heuristic that approximates the full eval suite used by release CI. Outputs are normalized into a small artifact that feeds rollout gate automation and LTS compatibility checks.

Why this matters:
- Current release validation relies on heavy centralized evals that often run late in the cycle; regressions found there are expensive to fix.
- Creating a concise, reproducible developer workflow increases detection velocity and reduces churn during release candidate stabilization and LTS backports.

Scope and goals:
- Define a declarative preflight policy format (preflight.yaml) capturing required smoke checks, perf thresholds, and allowed delta tolerances per LTS channel.
- Implement 'redwood-preflight' CLI that: (1) runs a compact smoke battery against a target runtime binary or container, (2) executes the Edge Sampler to produce 100–500 synthetic edge requests based on production signal profiles, (3) captures token-level latency percentiles and quality heuristics (e.g., ROUGE/minimal fuzz checks), and (4) emits an artifact (preflight.json) with normalized signals.
- Integrate artifact upload to preflight-store and add a gating step to canary rollouts: if multi-signal regression score > threshold, block rollout and create automated rollback ticket.
- Ensure the runner is fast (target < 10 minutes on dev workstation or CI small instance) and usable in local dev loops.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not replace full eval CI or release canary suites — it is an early warning tool aligned with, and calibrated to, existing evals.
acceptance_criteria: preflight.yaml schema documented with examples for LTS and stable channels
redwood-preflight CLI prototype that runs smoke checks + Edge Sampler and produces preflight.json
Edge Sampler produces representative synthetic requests from production profiles (100 samples) and includes a seedable mode
Artifact upload is validated in staging: preflight.json visible in preflight-store and linked to a release candidate
Gating integration: rollout automation reads preflight.json and enforces the configured multi-signal threshold
Local run completes within 10 minutes on CI small instance (2 vCPUs, 8GB RAM)
notes: Related ticket: ENG-997200 (rollout automation gate enforcement)
Edge Sampler approach: combine top-100 production prefixes, 20% synthetic adversarial variants, 10% long-tail outliers sampled by percentile-of-frequency
Data privacy: Edge Sampler must only use aggregated, anonymized request fingerprints; no PII payloads should be embedded in sample artifacts
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize preflight.yaml schema and minimal smoke battery definitions (token echo, basic chat flow, embedding consistency)
Week 2: implement redwood-preflight runner skeleton and basic smoke tests; wire preflight.json schema
Week 3: build Edge Sampler library and seedable generator; add quality heuristics (length consistency, top-k token diff)
Week 4: add artifact uploader and integration tests with preflight-store (staging); run calibration against last 3 release candidates
Week 5: integrate gating step into canary rollout automation and run pilot with runtime-1.22-rc1
Contingency: if sampling shows high false-positive rate, add auto-calibration pass that adjusts thresholds based on historical signal
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Local runs may not reflect canary production distribution. Mitigation: seed Edge Sampler with anonymized, high-level production fingerprints and include a 'canary-mode' that replays small live-sample buffers in staging.
Risk: Too many false positives cause gate fatigue. Mitigation: require multi-signal consensus (perf + quality + smoke) to block rollout and allow a manual override with audit trail.
Risk: Developers won't adopt CLI. Mitigation: integrate preflight into existing 'dev up' scripts and add VS Code task templates; ship a short onboarding doc and examples.
